title: POIGAI South India Climate & Ecology Knowledge Bank
scope: Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Puducherry and Lakshadweep. Neighbouring Western Ghats research is background only.
method: Curated evidence map, not an exhaustive review of all studies. Searches used government and original research organisations, research-team summaries and practitioner records. Review depth is stated per source. Search snippets and catalogues are explicitly distinguished from report excerpts. No full-text appraisal is claimed where access failed.

issues.title: Reliable village water
issues.places: Ramanathapuram; southern Tamil Nadu screening areas
issues.evidence: Groundwater resource and quality assessments are distinct evidence streams [S11]. Regional evidence cannot establish a particular village’s unmet need.
issues.response: Assess demand, leakage, storage and source quality first; compare repairs, safe rainwater capture and hydrogeologically suitable recharge. Reject recharge where contamination or saline conditions make it unsafe.
issues.baseline: Seasonal supply days, source tests, household collection time, extraction and recharge context.
issues.measure: Reliable supply days; tested water quality; collection time; operating cost.
issues.owner: Panchayat or utility with an explicitly appointed maintenance operator.
issues.gap: Exact village, household baseline, aquifer suitability and lifecycle budget unverified.

issues.title: Groundwater depletion in hard-rock catchments
issues.places: Interior Karnataka; Telangana plateau; Rayalaseema
issues.evidence: CGWB’s Karnataka assessment provides resource screening [S10]; Telangana’s state plan supplies sector context [S07]. Neither is a well-yield guarantee.
issues.response: Build a community water budget; meter large abstractions; align crops with dependable supply; assess managed recharge with a hydrogeologist and downstream users.
issues.baseline: Seasonal water levels, abstraction, well failures and water quality.
issues.measure: Water-level trend over comparable seasons; extraction; irrigation water per unit output.
issues.owner: Groundwater department, panchayat and participating water users.
issues.gap: Assessment-unit tables and present village surveys still needed.

issues.title: Urban lakes and sewage inflows
issues.places: Bengaluru lake catchments; Jakkur as a documented case
issues.evidence: Jakkur’s practitioner account describes treated and untreated inflows, vegetation work and multiple maintenance institutions [S20].
issues.response: Trace every inlet; intercept pollution; verify treatment compliance; evaluate wetlands as polishing stages with ongoing maintenance, rather than substitutes for sewage treatment.
issues.baseline: Inlet flows and pollutant loads; seasonal lake chemistry; treatment uptime.
issues.measure: Compliant inflows; oxygen and nutrient trends; recurring maintenance completed.
issues.owner: Utility, lake custodian and contracted operator, with community oversight.
issues.gap: 2018 case observations are not current lake measurements or a causal impact trial.

issues.title: Flood pathways and wetland storage
issues.places: Chennai basin; Hyderabad; Bengaluru; Puducherry urban catchments
issues.evidence: Flood studies require rainfall, drainage, land-use and exposure evidence together. The Chennai event summary cautions against treating flood damage as rainfall attribution [S15].
issues.response: Map drainage and flood storage at catchment scale; protect water pathways; assess retention areas, maintenance and accessible evacuation routes. Check whether interventions shift flooding downstream.
issues.baseline: Drain connectivity, observed inundation depth and duration, vulnerable assets and rainfall.
issues.measure: Inundation duration under comparable storms; protected routes; warning reach.
issues.owner: Urban local body, drainage authority and disaster-management teams.
issues.gap: Hydraulic modelling and local consent needed before earthworks.

issues.title: Landslide exposure in the Western Ghats
issues.places: Wayanad; Nilgiris; Kodagu as separate screening landscapes
issues.evidence: The 2024 Wayanad assessment found intensified triggering rain with substantial modelling uncertainty [S14]. It does not establish the cause of every slope failure.
issues.response: Use official susceptibility maps, geotechnical inspection and local rainfall thresholds; prioritise evacuation access and exposure reduction. Retaining structures need engineered designs.
issues.baseline: Slope geology, past failures, drainage, rainfall and households in runout paths.
issues.measure: Warning-to-action time; evacuation drills; people and assets removed from high exposure.
issues.owner: District disaster authority, qualified geotechnical team and local government.
issues.gap: Transfer from Wayanad to other slopes requires independent validation.

issues.title: Hot classrooms and public buildings
issues.places: Tiruchirappalli concept; hot urban and peri-urban institutions
issues.evidence: Telangana’s cool-roof policy defines material-performance provisions [S09]; it is policy evidence, not measured results for a particular school.
issues.response: Compare reflective roofs, external shade, safe ventilation and efficient cooling. Inspect waterproofing, structure, glare, maintenance and indoor air quality before retrofit.
issues.baseline: Paired indoor/outdoor temperature and humidity logs; occupancy; roof condition; electricity.
issues.measure: Occupied hours above an agreed comfort threshold; comparable indoor temperature; kWh.
issues.owner: Building owner with facilities operator and qualified designer.
issues.gap: Building selection, hot-weather comparison and costed specifications pending.

issues.title: Outdoor workers and unequal heat exposure
issues.places: Construction sites, markets, farms and transport hubs
issues.evidence: State climate plans address health and livelihoods [S06, S07]. Air temperature alone does not capture all occupational exposure.
issues.response: Have occupational-health professionals design shade, rest, safe drinking-water access and warning procedures. Adapt work schedules with workers, protect wages and provide an emergency response protocol.
issues.baseline: Task and exposure mapping; humidity and radiant heat; access to shade and water.
issues.measure: Protected work periods; warning coverage; recorded heat incidents with reporting quality checked.
issues.owner: Employer and local authority with worker representatives and health teams.
issues.gap: No medical threshold or clinical advice is inferred from this bank.

issues.title: Shoreline erosion and coastal livelihoods
issues.places: Coromandel and Malabar coasts; Puducherry and Karaikal
issues.evidence: NCCR’s official summary reports shoreline change from both human and natural drivers [S17]. Historic erosion rates do not forecast an individual property’s future.
issues.response: Commission sediment-cell and hazard assessment; compare setbacks, dune recovery, relocation support and engineered protection. Evaluate neighbouring-shore impacts and fishing access.
issues.baseline: Shoreline positions, seasonal beach profiles, structures, access and land tenure.
issues.measure: Beach-profile trend; maintained livelihood access; exposure avoided.
issues.owner: Coastal authority and local government with fishing communities.
issues.gap: Permits, sediment budget and long-term maintenance must be resolved.

issues.title: Cyclones, surge and delta settlements
issues.places: Krishna and Godavari deltas; coastal Tamil Nadu; Yanam and Karaikal
issues.evidence: State profiles identify differing cyclone, surge and river settings [S06, S08]. Hazard combinations vary by location.
issues.response: Map compound river–rain–surge exposure; strengthen last-mile warning, inclusive shelters and resilient essential services. Validate any ecosystem buffer against local habitat and hydrology.
issues.baseline: Elevation, evacuation travel time, warning reach, essential-service exposure.
issues.measure: Accessible shelter coverage; drill completion; service restoration time.
issues.owner: District disaster authority, local government and utility owners.
issues.gap: Current official hazard maps and facility audits needed.

issues.title: Reefs and marine heatwaves
issues.places: Lakshadweep; Gulf of Mannar for separate monitoring
issues.evidence: The official 2024 response records Lakshadweep bleaching and INCOIS monitoring services [S24, S25]. This is not a current Gulf of Mannar condition report.
issues.response: Use dated bleaching alerts and ecological surveys; reduce local sewage, anchor and extraction damage; agree community-led response. Restoration cannot remove ocean warming.
issues.baseline: Reef-cover transects, temperature stress, local pressures and fishing dependence.
issues.measure: Live coral and recruitment trends; reduced damaging activity; livelihood resilience.
issues.owner: Relevant reef and fisheries authorities with island or coastal communities.
issues.gap: Reef-specific condition and recovery evidence needed before restoration claims.

issues.title: Dryland crops under erratic rainfall
issues.places: Historical Anantapur region; interior dryland farming belts
issues.evidence: ICAR’s vulnerability atlas and NICRA catalogue support agricultural screening and technology selection [S12, S13]; local effect sizes are not extracted here.
issues.response: Co-design crop calendars, locally suited varieties, soil-moisture conservation and diversified cropping with KVK agronomists. Test small plots before wider adoption.
issues.baseline: Crop-wise yields, dry spells, soil moisture, input costs and labour.
issues.measure: Yield stability across seasons; net margin; crop-failure frequency.
issues.owner: Farmer group or FPO with KVK and agreed field support.
issues.gap: Current district boundaries, farmer cluster and two-season evaluation design needed.

issues.title: Natural farming: test benefits and trade-offs
issues.places: Crop-specific farmer trials in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka
issues.evidence: ICAR’s survey and sample study reports differing experiences between crops and states [S21]. Farmer perception and adopter comparisons do not establish universal causal benefits.
issues.response: Use comparable plots and whole-farm records to evaluate input reduction, nutrient balance, pest management and transition labour. Preserve farmer choice and avoid guaranteed yield or income claims.
issues.baseline: Crop and soil comparability; prior yield; purchased and household inputs; labour.
issues.measure: Net return including labour; yield variability; soil indicators; adoption retention.
issues.owner: Participating farmers, independent agronomist and evaluation team.
issues.gap: Selection bias, market premiums and long-term nutrient balance need explicit treatment.

issues.title: Farm ponds and watershed interventions
issues.places: Semi-arid catchments; location selected after hydrology
issues.evidence: ICAR-CRIDA lists farm-pond design guidance [S13]. A catalogue listing does not prove a pond is suitable or beneficial at every farm.
issues.response: Assess catchment water balance, soils, safety, evaporation and downstream rights; compare in-situ conservation with storage and supplemental irrigation.
issues.baseline: Runoff, seasonal demand, soils, evaporation and downstream users.
issues.measure: Supplemental water delivered; crop benefit; maintenance; downstream effects.
issues.owner: Farmer group and watershed institution with engineering support.
issues.gap: No storage volume or construction budget should be set before survey.

issues.title: Land degradation and soil loss
issues.places: Erosion-prone slopes and degraded cultivated catchments
issues.evidence: SAC–ISRO provides land-degradation mapping and change-analysis resources [S18]. Remote-sensing categories need ground verification.
issues.response: Identify the degradation process first; assess contour measures, ground cover and appropriate grazing or cultivation changes. Protect drainage and land-user rights.
issues.baseline: Erosion features, soil depth, cover, infiltration and land-use history.
issues.measure: Ground cover; soil loss proxy; infiltration; productive use maintained.
issues.owner: Land users and watershed authority with soil-conservation specialists.
issues.gap: Field diagnosis needed; a degraded-land label is not permission for plantation.

issues.title: Native habitats and invasive plants
issues.places: Nilgiris and other Western Ghats landscapes
issues.evidence: ATREE documents landscape-specific restoration and invasive-species research [S22]. Intervention success depends on habitat, disturbance and follow-up.
issues.response: Map native habitat and invasion; pilot species-appropriate removal with native recovery, erosion control and repeat monitoring. Budget follow-up before scaling.
issues.baseline: Native species, invasive cover, regeneration and community resource use.
issues.measure: Native recovery; invasive rebound; habitat function and livelihood effects.
issues.owner: Forest or habitat custodian, restoration ecologist and rights-holding communities.
issues.gap: Removal-only campaigns and sapling counts cannot establish restoration success.

issues.title: Grasslands are ecosystems too
issues.places: Montane grasslands and Deccan open natural ecosystems
issues.evidence: ATREE’s grassland initiative recognises ecological and pastoral value [S23]. Open landscapes must not automatically be treated as empty land.
issues.response: Verify historic habitat, native species and customary grazing; protect suitable open ecosystems. Evaluate restoration with botanists and land users before adding trees.
issues.baseline: Habitat history, native cover, birds and plants, grazing use and tenure.
issues.measure: Native habitat retained; species recovery; pastoral access maintained.
issues.owner: Habitat custodian, ecologist and pastoral or community representatives.
issues.gap: Site-specific conservation design and rights assessment required.

issues.title: Sewage treatment that actually operates
issues.places: Urban and peri-urban settlements; receiving rivers and lakes
issues.evidence: CPCB distinguishes installed, operational and compliant treatment [S19]. Its 2020 inventory is historical.
issues.response: Measure real flows and pollution loads; repair collection and treatment bottlenecks; plan safe sludge management and verified reuse demand with funded operations.
issues.baseline: Connected flows, bypasses, effluent tests, energy and operator capacity.
issues.measure: Compliant treated flow; bypass frequency; verified safe reuse.
issues.owner: Utility or local body with accountable plant operator.
issues.gap: Current plant tests, permits and full operating budget required.

issues.title: Organic waste, dumpsites and methane
issues.places: Municipalities, markets and institutional campuses
issues.evidence: CPCB’s 2021–22 report records state processing and dumpsite information [S26]. Reported facilities do not demonstrate today’s processing quality.
issues.response: Audit composition and actual material flows; segregate at source; compare composting, digestion and safe residual disposal. Include worker safety, leachate, odour and product off-take.
issues.baseline: Weighed waste streams, contamination, disposal routes and operating costs.
issues.measure: Verified diversion; contamination; processing uptime; methane leakage where relevant.
issues.owner: Local body and operator with waste-worker participation.
issues.gap: Avoid counting collected tonnage as treated tonnage or unverified carbon savings.

issues.title: Efficient buildings and cleaner energy
issues.places: Public buildings, SMEs and residential clusters
issues.evidence: IPCC’s global assessment supports efficiency and cleaner energy [S27]; local savings need building-level measurement.
issues.response: Audit loads; address avoidable demand and efficiency; assess rooftop solar, cooling equipment and refrigerant management. Check roof safety and lifecycle disposal.
issues.baseline: Metered electricity, occupancy, equipment and structural condition.
issues.measure: Weather-adjusted kWh; lifecycle costs; emissions using a disclosed factor.
issues.owner: Asset owner, qualified energy professional and maintenance contractor.
issues.gap: No payback, tariff or emissions factor is assumed.

issues.title: Accessible low-carbon travel
issues.places: Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kochi and secondary cities
issues.evidence: IPCC transport findings support public and active travel [S28]. They do not quantify savings for a particular Indian corridor.
issues.response: Assess safe shaded walking, universal access, connected transit and suitable fleet electrification together. Evaluate demand, grid emissions and access for lower-income users.
issues.baseline: Travel patterns, safety, fares, vehicle occupancy and energy use.
issues.measure: Reliable access; mode shift; avoided vehicle-km; lifecycle emissions.
issues.owner: Transport authority and local body with commuters and accessibility groups.
issues.gap: Route feasibility and local lifecycle comparison needed.

issues.title: District evidence before funding
issues.places: Every proposed district, village or institutional project
issues.evidence: CEEW’s vulnerability method combines exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity [S02]. A composite ranking cannot replace a local baseline.
issues.response: Document the exact place, baseline, unmet need, implementation partner, maintenance owner, costed design and measurable outcome. Agree consent, safeguards, procurement and reporting before funding.
issues.baseline: Dated local measurements, affected groups, existing services and counterfactual.
issues.measure: Outcome against baseline; distribution of benefits; full costs and maintenance.
issues.owner: Named project proponent and independent reviewer; appointments require acceptance.
issues.gap: No intervention here is a validated or funded POIGAI project.

issues.title: Choose evidence at the right scale
issues.places: Regional assessment → district screening → site design
issues.evidence: MoES synthesises observed and projected regional climate [S01]. Scenario outputs, weather forecasts and measured local conditions answer different questions.
issues.response: Keep observation periods, scenarios, model resolution and uncertainty visible. Use multiple relevant datasets and technical review; investigate disagreements rather than averaging incompatible risk indices.
issues.baseline: Source year, geography, methods, scenario and data quality.
issues.measure: Traceable claims; reproducible baselines; documented uncertainty and correction history.
issues.owner: Knowledge editor and relevant subject specialist.
issues.gap: This edition screens selected sources and does not claim an exhaustive systematic review.
